<Short>
Pick a password manager, move your passwords in, and [delete the export](#delete-the-export) once it's done.
</Short>

## Pick one

Any of these will do the job, and they're in the list's order.

<Picks section="Password Managers" limit={3} skip={['lesspass']} />

If you're leaving <Swap product="lastpass">LastPass</Swap>, <App name="Bitwarden" /> imports its export directly. A <Term slug="zero-knowledge">zero-knowledge</Term> design means the company can't read your vault.

## Move your passwords in

<Tip id="delete-the-export" priority="essential" effort={1} title="Delete the export file once it's imported">
Your browser's export is a plain text file with every password you've got in it.[^1]

<Steps>
1. Open <Path>Settings --> Passwords --> Export</Path> in your browser.
2. Import the file, then delete it and empty the bin.
</Steps>
</Tip>

<Tip id="turn-off-browser-saving" priority="optional" effort={2} title="Turn off your browser's own password saving">
Otherwise your passwords end up in two places, and you'll change one and forget the other.

<Platforms>
<Platform name="ios">
Open <Path>Settings --> Apps --> Passwords</Path>.
</Platform>
<Platform name="android">
Open <Path>Settings --> Google --> Autofill</Path>.
</Platform>
</Platforms>
</Tip>

<Tip id="check-old-exports" priority="advanced" effort={10} title="Look for old exports you've forgotten about">
<Note kind="warning">
An export from years ago is still a list of passwords, and some of them probably still work.
</Note>

<Region place="uk">
The NCSC has its own advice on this, which is worth a read.[^2]
</Region>
</Tip>

<Note kind="info">
It's worth doing the five accounts that matter most first --> then the rest as you go.
</Note>

[^1]: [Chrome Help: Export your passwords](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95606)
[^2]: [NCSC: Password managers](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/top-tips-for-staying-secure-online/password-managers)
